subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A test is administered only once. The teacher then divides the test into odd-numbered and even-numbered items, scores each half separately, and correlates the two sets of scores to estimate reliability. This method is called:
explanation: Split-half reliability estimates internal consistency from a single administration, unlike test-retest (two administrations over time) or parallel-forms (two equivalent versions).

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Two different but equivalent versions of the same test (matched in content, difficulty, and length) are administered to the same group, and the scores on both versions are correlated to check consistency. This method of estimating reliability is called:
explanation: Parallel-forms reliability uses two equivalent test versions on the same group to check consistency, avoiding memory/practice effects.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Over the year, a student compiles a purposeful collection of their best written work, art projects, and reflective notes, showing growth and effort over time, which the teacher reviews periodically instead of relying only on term-end exams. This assessment tool is called a:
explanation: A portfolio is a purposeful, ongoing collection of a student's work samples documenting growth over time — a key CCE tool.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Before grading student essays, a teacher prepares a scoring guide that clearly describes what performance looks like at each level (e.g., 'excellent', 'good', 'needs improvement') for criteria like organisation, argument, and grammar, ensuring consistent and transparent grading. This scoring guide is called a:
explanation: A rubric is a scoring guide listing explicit criteria and performance-level descriptors for consistent, transparent grading.

stem: A good educational test is expected to give the same score regardless of who scores it (not depending on the examiner's personal judgement or mood). This essential characteristic of a good test is known as:
explanation: Objectivity means scoring is free from examiner bias — distinct from reliability (consistency) and validity (measures what it claims to).
